title: Iconography / Overview

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; interactive elements retain their captured state

slide_intent: Match a symbol’s detail and role to its context, so people can distinguish an action, a product and a broader idea at a glance.
strategic_value: A related family of UI icons, app icons and pictograms can give IBM recognizable visual continuity without forcing every task into one symbol style.
demonstration: The page introduces three icon types through a blue media state, a comparison sheet, three principle rows and separate UI, app and pictogram specimen grids.
practical_value: Choose UI icons for interface actions, app icons for product identification and pictograms for broader concepts.

content_islands.name: System introduction
content_islands.spec: Place the Overview heading and role explanation above the blue icon-film state.

content_islands.name: Comparative vocabulary
content_islands.spec: Show UI icons, app icons and pictograms together before the Engineered, Clear and Nimble principle rows.

content_islands.name: UI and app specimens
content_islands.spec: Present separate gridded examples with paragraphs describing functional actions and product identification.

content_islands.name: Pictogram range
content_islands.spec: Close with the productive/expressive distinction and the captured productive pictogram tab.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explains how icon types simplify messages and why different contexts need different detail.
reference_purposes.Expression: The three specimen sets show shared precision with different degrees of color and detail.
reference_purposes.Application: The text assigns UI icons to functional actions, app icons to product identification and pictograms to broader concepts.

inspection.method: Six uniformly spaced sampled frames across the complete clip
